subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat `all | final | off` tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety rule should apply to failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: Source inspection proves the remaining gap, but choosing whether UX suppression can override the current failed-mutation safety fallback is a product/config decision rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep boolean suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow remaining work to docs or channel-specific leaks.

options.title: Split by warning family
options.body: Defer a general enum and handle remaining leaks, routing needs, or channel aggregates in narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged warning-policy work is closest to the unresolved safety/default decision and explicitly left this issue open for the broader policy.
